allowed_dependency_manifest.content: Let n, k, l ∈ Z with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n. Define R(q) = [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q in the natural rational-function setting for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. If R(q) lies in a polynomial ring in q (i.e., R(q) has only finitely many nonnegative powers of q with coefficients in the relevant coefficient ring), then when written as R(q) = Σ_i c_i q^i, every coefficient c_i satisfies c_i ≥ 0.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.statement_nl: Let M = direct sum_{m >= 0} M_m be a graded Q-vector space such that every homogeneous component M_m is finite-dimensional over Q. Define Hilb_M(q) := sum_{m >= 0} (dim_Q M_m) q^m in Q[[q]]. Then every coefficient of Hilb_M(q) is a nonnegative integer. In particular, if Hilb_M(q) actually lies in Q[q], then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

result_payload.proof_nl:
By definition of the Hilbert series,

Hilb_M(q) = \sum_{m\ge 0} (\dim_\mathbb{Q} M_m) q^m \in \mathbb{Q}[[q]].

Now, in a formal power series \(\sum_{m\ge 0} a_m q^m\), the coefficient of \(q^m\) is exactly \(a_m\). Therefore, for each integer \(m\ge 0\), the coefficient of \(q^m\) in \(\operatorname{Hilb}_M(q)\) is

\[\dim_\mathbb{Q}(M_m).\]

Since each \(M_m\) is finite-dimensional over \(\mathbb{Q}\), its dimension is a well-defined nonnegative integer. Hence every coefficient of \(\operatorname{Hilb}_M(q)\) lies in \(\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\).

This proves the first claim.

For the second claim, assume in addition that \(\operatorname{Hilb}_M(q)\in \mathbb{Q}[q]\). Then the same series has only finitely many nonzero coefficients, but each coefficient is still the coefficient of some \(q^m\) in \(\operatorname{Hilb}_M(q)\), hence equals \(\dim_\mathbb{Q}(M_m)\) for that \(m\), and is therefore in \(\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\). Coefficients of degrees not appearing are \(0\), which is also nonnegative. So that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

Thus every coefficient of \(\operatorname{Hilb}_M(q)\) is a nonnegative integer, and in particular, if \(\operatorname{Hilb}_M(q)\) is a polynomial, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.
result_payload.proof_summary: The Hilbert series is defined as \(\sum_{m\ge0}(\dim_\mathbb{Q} M_m)q^m\), so by definition the coefficient of \(q^m\) is \(\dim_\mathbb{Q} M_m\). Each \(M_m\) is finite-dimensional, so this dimension is a nonnegative integer. If the series is actually a polynomial, the same coefficient statement still holds, and missing coefficients are 0.
